chunks: And Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, عليهما السلام, who said:

"The sunnah (prophetic tradition) for the people of the cities is that they go out from their cities on the two Eids, except the people of Makkah, for they perform salat (prayer) in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām."

key_terms.أَهْلَ مَكَّةَ: the people of Makkah, who are excepted from the general rule
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْأَمْصَارِ: the inhabitants of the cities or settled urban communities
key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the normative prophetic tradition or established religious practice
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two Eid festivals, Eid al-Fiṭr and Eid al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.يَبْرُزُوا: to go out to an open area outside the city

ai.seo_question: Where should the people of cities and the people of Makkah perform the Eid salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states the sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding the salat (prayer) of the two Eids for the inhabitants of cities: they should go out to an open place outside their urban area. An exception is made for the people of Makkah, whose Eid salat (prayer) is performed in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1466 - Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father (as) that He said:
"The Sunnah (tradition) for the people of cities is to go out from their cities for the two Eid prayers, except for the people of Mecca, who pray in the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram)."
